description: Key facts a correct lesson on each Digital Logic Design topic must state. Every fact was taken from the fetched text of the source page named with it (the quote is checked by `npm run golden:check`). Patterns are case-insensitive regular expressions matched against the lesson text after LaTeX backslashes and braces are removed.
subject: digital-logic

facts.claim: Rows and columns follow Gray code

source.quote: The row and column indices (shown across the top and down the left side of the Karnaugh map) are ordered in Gray code

facts.claim: Group adjacent 1s to simplify

source.quote: Adjacent 1s in the Karnaugh map represent opportunities to simplify the expression

facts.claim: A multiplexer selects one of several inputs using select lines

source.quote: The selection is directed by a separate set of digital inputs known as select lines

facts.claim: A demultiplexer sends one input to one of several outputs

source.quote: a demultiplexer (or demux) is a device that takes a single input signal and selectively forwards it to one of several output lines

facts.claim: A full adder adds a carry in as well

source.quote: A full adder adds binary numbers and accounts for values carried in as well as out

facts.claim: Two half adders plus an OR gate make a full adder

source.quote: two half adders can be combined to make a full adder

facts.claim: Two stable states; stores one bit

source.quote: flip-flops and latches are circuits that have two stable states

facts.claim: Flip-flops change on a clock edge; latches are level-triggered

source.quote: an edge-triggered flip-flop's output only changes on a clock edge

facts.claim: A counter counts clock transitions, built from flip-flops

source.quote: A counter typically consists of flip-flops, which store a value representing the current count

facts.claim: Number of flip-flops sets the maximum modulus

source.quote: The maximum possible modulus of a counter is determined by the number of flip-flops

facts.claim: A cascade of flip-flops, each output feeding the next input

source.quote: using a cascade of flip-flops where the output of one flip-flop is connected to the input of the next

facts.claim: A shared clock shifts the data one place

source.quote: They share a single clock signal, which causes the data stored in the system to shift from one location to the next

facts.claim: An FSM is in exactly one of a finite number of states
facts.pattern: finite number of states|one state at a time|exactly one

source.quote: It is an abstract machine that can be in exactly one of a finite number of states at any given time

facts.claim: Moving between states is a transition

source.quote: the change from one state to another is called a transition

facts.claim: TTL is built from bipolar junction transistors

source.quote: Transistor–transistor logic (TTL) is a logic family built from bipolar junction transistors (BJTs)

facts.claim: An FPGA is reprogrammable after manufacturing

source.quote: is a type of configurable integrated circuit that can be repeatedly programmed after manufacturing

facts.claim: Made of configurable logic blocks

source.quote: They consist of a grid-connected array of programmable logic blocks

facts.claim: BCD codes each decimal digit in four bits

source.quote: each decimal digit is represented by its corresponding four-bit binary value

facts.claim: ROM is non-volatile

source.quote: Read-only memory (ROM) is a form of non-volatile memory

facts.claim: RAM is volatile: it loses data when power is off

source.quote: RAM, or random access memory, is a temporary, volatile storage medium that loses data when the system powers down

facts.claim: VHDL is a hardware description language

source.quote: VHDL (VHSIC hardware description language) is a hardware description language

facts.claim: Designs are simulated before synthesis

source.quote: allows the behavior of the required system to be described (modeled) and verified (simulated) before synthesis
